entries.content:
Done. 

**Root cause / feature:** Hydra had no `env` config group, so users had no built-in way to swap "environment" defaults (e.g. provide default callbacks or override `hydra.run.dir`) via a config group.

**Fix:** Added a new `hydra/env` config group to Hydra's own config:
1. Created `hydra/conf/hydra/env/default.yaml` (`# @package hydra.env`), an empty default option for the group.
2. In `hydra/conf/__init__.py`, added `{"env": "default"}` to `HydraConf.defaults` (before `{"callbacks": None}`) and added the corresponding `env: Any = MISSING` field to the `HydraConf` structured config so the group composes cleanly.

This makes `hydra/env=default` part of every composed config (visible in `hydra.choices` and `--cfg hydra` as `env: {}`), and users can now override it with their own `hydra/env/*.yaml` configs — either with `# @package hydra.env` to set env-specific values, or `# @package hydra` to change defaults like `run.dir` or default callbacks. Verified via composition tests (both package styles), plus updated existing expectations in `tests/test_config_loader.py` (choices and `list_groups`) and `tests/test_completion.py`; full runs of `test_config_loader.py`, `test_completion.py`, `test_hydra.py`, `test_compose.py`, `test_callbacks.py`, `test_basic_launcher.py` and related example tests all pass.
